description:
Navratri 2026 (11–19 October) — Maa Durga ke 9 roop, har Devi ka mahatva (significance), katha aur day-wise mantra, ek hi video mein.
Watch the significance, then chant along every morning of Navratri.

Why this video: Navratri ke 9 roop ek journey hain — steadiness (Shailaputri) → discipline (Brahmacharini) → courage (Chandraghanta) → creation (Kushmanda) → mother's love (Skandamata) → victory (Katyayani) → freedom from fear (Kalaratri) → purity (Mahagauri) → fulfilment (Siddhidatri).

01:30 Day 1 · Shailaputri — mahatva + mantra
05:30 Day 2 · Brahmacharini — mahatva + mantra

29:30 Day 8 · Mahagauri — mahatva + mantra
33:30 Day 9 · Siddhidatri — mahatva + mantra

40:00 Vijayadashami + Durga Aarti

Dates: Navratri starts 11 Oct 2026 (Ghatasthapana), Vijayadashami 20 Oct. Ashtami/Navami timing can vary by city — check your local panchang.
Mantras and aarti are traditional (public domain). Stories as per Devi Mahatmya / popular Puranic tradition.

#Navratri2026 #Navdurga #DurgaMaa

format.length: 40–45 min (mantra jukebox with a 60–90 sec significance segment before each Devi)
format.hook: Navratri ke 9 din sirf 9 roop nahi, ek poori journey hain — Shailaputri ki stability se Siddhidatri ki siddhi tak. Aaj jaaniye har Devi ka mahatva, aur saath mein chant kijiye unka mantra.
outline: Intro (60 sec): why Navratri — Durga's 9-night battle and victory over Mahishasura, Vijayadashami on 20 Oct; the 9 roop are the 9 steps of one sadhana (Devi Kavach, Durga Saptashati: 'Prathamam Shailaputri...')

Day 1 · Shailaputri (11 Oct, orange) — Significance (60–90 sec): daughter of Himalaya (Parvati reborn after Sati); rides Nandi, trident + lotus. Meaning: Foundation and steadiness — the root of the whole Navratri sadhana. Then mantra 'ॐ देवी शैलपुत्र्यै नमः' ×11 + short stuti

Day 2 · Brahmacharini (12 Oct, white) — Significance (60–90 sec): Parvati's years of tapasya for Shiva, living on bilva leaves and water; japa mala + kamandalu. Meaning: Tapas, discipline and focus — perfect for students and anyone starting a vrat. Then mantra 'ॐ देवी ब्रह्मचारिण्यै नमः' ×11 + short stuti

Day 3 · Chandraghanta (13 Oct, red) — Significance (60–90 sec): half-moon shaped like a bell on her forehead; rides a tiger, ten arms with weapons, form taken after marriage to Shiva. Meaning: Courage and protection — the sound of her ghanta drives away fear. Then mantra 'ॐ देवी चन्द्रघण्टायै नमः' ×11 + short stuti

Day 4 · Kushmanda (14 Oct, royal blue) — Significance (60–90 sec): creates the cosmic egg (brahmanda) with her gentle smile; source of the sun's light and warmth. Meaning: Energy, health and fresh creation. Then mantra 'ॐ देवी कूष्माण्डायै नमः' ×11 + short stuti

Day 5 · Skandamata (15 Oct, yellow) — Significance (60–90 sec): mother of Skanda (Kartikeya), holds him on her lap, rides a lion. Meaning: Mother's love and wisdom — family well-being and blessings for children. Then mantra 'ॐ देवी स्कन्दमातायै नमः' ×11 + short stuti

Day 6 · Katyayani (16 Oct, green) — Significance (60–90 sec): born in Sage Katyayana's ashram; the warrior form that defeats Mahishasura. Meaning: Victory over negativity; traditionally prayed to for a good life partner. Then mantra 'ॐ देवी कात्यायन्यै नमः' ×11 + short stuti

Day 7 · Kalaratri (17 Oct, grey) — Significance (60–90 sec): fierce dark form who destroys Raktabija so his blood cannot create new demons. Meaning: Freedom from fear and darkness — fierce outside, protective inside (also called Shubhankari). Then mantra 'ॐ देवी कालरात्र्यै नमः' ×11 + short stuti

Day 8 · Mahagauri (Ashtami, purple) — Significance (60–90 sec): radiant white form after tapasya; rides a white bull, trident + damaru. Meaning: Purity, peace and a fresh start; Ashtami is the day of Kanya Pujan in many homes. Then mantra 'ॐ देवी महागौर्यै नमः' ×11 + short stuti

Day 9 · Siddhidatri (Navami, peacock green) — Significance (60–90 sec): giver of all siddhis, seated on a lotus; even Shiva received siddhis from her. Meaning: Completion — the fruit of all nine days of sadhana. Then mantra 'ॐ देवी सिद्धिदात्र्यै नमः' ×11 + short stuti
Why the 9 colours: a modern popular custom tied to the weekday Navratri starts on (changes every year), not a scriptural rule — say this honestly
Close: Vijayadashami meaning (victory of good over evil — Durga over Mahishasura, Rama over Ravana) + Durga aarti 'Jai Ambe Gauri' (traditional)
shorts: One 45–60 sec Short per day at 5:30 AM: 'Aaj ki Devi' — 1-line story, what she blesses, colour, and the mantra ×3
Short: 'Navratri ke 9 roop = 9 steps of sadhana' (the journey in 50 sec)
Short: 'Kalaratri darawni kyun dikhti hain?' — Raktabija story and why she is also Shubhankari
Colour-of-the-day Short for women's audience (outfit colour, with the honest note that colours are a custom)

risk_flags: Ashtami and Navami may both fall on Mon 19 Oct in some panchangs (tithi overlap) while colour lists show Day 8 = 18 Oct — don't print dates for Day 8/9 in the video, say 'Ashtami'/'Navami' and tell viewers to check local panchang. Present stories as tradition ('maana jaata hai'), avoid claims like 'this mantra will change your life'. Colours are a modern custom — say so. Use only traditional mantras/aarti or own recordings; original or licensed Devi art.
